title: Hiring demographics audit
description: Audit a hiring dataset for adverse impact across demographic dimensions and job roles — computes four-fifths ratios, dual significance testing (Fisher's exact + chi-square), and produces a narrative compliance report backed by a structured metrics table, with a hard programmatic-validation gate and a fact-check gate that verifies the executive summary's numbers against the metrics CSV before the run is allowed to pass.

cta.label: Fork and run
cta.note: Runs on Jetty's managed sandbox. No setup. Free for your first 10 runs.

example_outputs.title: Regional healthcare network — 900 synthetic candidates, 6 roles
example_outputs.summary: A 900-candidate synthetic dataset with two deliberately injected disparities (Lab Technician candidates aged 50+, Hispanic/Latino Clinic Administrator candidates). Both surface in disparity_metrics.csv at four-fifths ratios of 0.48 and 0.15; 57 cells flagged in total, all 10 programmatic checks and the summary fact-check gate pass, rubric 5.0/5 in a single pass.

outputs.description: Narrative compliance/fairness report for HR/legal review — methodology, findings by role and dimension, flagged items with both p-values, recommendations, caveats.
125 rows — one per (role, dimension, group) plus ALL_ROLES rollups — with counts, selection rates, four-fifths ratios, dual significance tests, flags.
Executive summary; flagged count and top-5 findings re-derived from the CSV by the Step 9 gate.
10 programmatic checks, summary-accuracy gate, six rubric scores, overall_passed.

example_outputs.title: Synthetic CV dataset (1,000 candidates, 12 roles)
example_outputs.summary: A full audit over 1,000 synthetic candidates across 12 job roles and 5 protected attributes, scoring 5.0/5 on the rubric with every programmatic check and the fact-check gate passing.

outputs.description: Narrative compliance/fairness report for HR/legal review.
Structured per-(role, dimension, group) metrics table with four-fifths ratios and dual significance tests.
Programmatic checks, summary-accuracy gate, and rubric scores.

inputs.label: Input dataset
inputs.description: CSV, one row per candidate, including job role applied for, hiring outcome, and demographic columns.

inputs.label: Protected attributes
inputs.description: Comma-separated demographic columns/dimensions to analyze for disparity.

inputs.label: Job role field
inputs.description: Column name identifying the job role/req the candidate applied for.

inputs.label: Disparity threshold
inputs.description: Four-fifths rule threshold below which a group is flagged.

inputs.label: Minimum group size
inputs.description: Minimum cell size before a significance test is attempted.

metrics._note: Live counters — supplied by the Jetty backend at render time, not authored here.

caveats: Statistical disparity flagged by the four-fifths rule and significance tests does not by itself establish discriminatory intent — see the report's own caveats section.
The sample dataset is synthetic and used for audit-methodology demonstration only, not a real EEOC/OFCCP filing.

Rubric scores are self-assessed by the agent, though gated by a hard programmatic-validation step (Step 4) and a fact-check step (Step 9) that verify calculations and summary numbers against the CSV rather than relying on impression alone.

The reference group for the four-fifths ratio is the highest-selection-rate group in each (role, dimension) cell regardless of its size, so a tiny group hired at 100% (e.g. 2 candidates) becomes the reference and pushes every sibling group into flagged + low_confidence. The healthcare-network-run example shows this: its injected Clinic Administrator disparity is flagged at ratio 0.15 but marked low-confidence for exactly that reason. Read low_confidence rows directionally, or raise min_group_size, until a future runbook version restricts reference-group selection to groups meeting min_group_size.
